issues.failure_explanation: The corollary inverts \hat{\Xi}_t and calibrates the ellipsoid with the \chi^2_d quantile (and intervals with Gaussian quantiles), which presupposes \Xi^\star \succ 0 (and w^T\Xi^\star w>0). Assumptions 1-4 only impose upper bounds on noise moments (growth conditions (ass:2:4th), (ass:3:4th)); nothing rules out rank-deficient gradient noise at x*. E.g., noise with \nabla f(x*;\xi) supported on a proper subspace satisfies all assumptions but makes \Omega^\star, hence \Lambda=\mE[(I-\tilde C^\star)\Omega^\star(I-\tilde C^\star)^T] and \Xi^\star=U(\Theta\circ U^T\Lambda U)U^T, singular. Then \hat{\Xi}_t is asymptotically degenerate, \hat{\Xi}_t^{-1} diverges along null directions, the pivot does not converge to \chi^2_d, and the stated 1-q coverage limits fail in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard nondegeneracy hypothesis \mE[\nabla f(x*;\xi)\nabla f(x*;\xi)^T] \succ 0 (so \Omega^\star \succ 0; with full-support sketching \Lambda \succ 0, and since \Theta is a positive Cauchy-type matrix, \Xi^\star \succ 0 by the Schur product theorem); \hat{\Xi}_t is then invertible with probability tending to 1 and both statements go through.
issues.overall_effect: Both displays of Corollary sec4:cor1 (the ellipsoidal confidence region and the directional intervals) are not valid as stated over the full hypothesis class; the subsequent 'fully online and matrix-free' inference paragraph built on \hat{\Xi}_t^{-1} inherits the same gap.
issues.title: Confidence-region and interval guarantees omit any positive-definiteness requirement on the limiting covariance Xi*
issues.why_classification: The repair adds one standard local nondegeneracy condition; the estimator, method, rates, and advertised inference scope all survive unchanged, and no new nontrivial lemma is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem sec4:thm1's bound for beta>0.5 is 1/\sqrt{t\beta_t} + \chi_t/\beta_t^{1.5}, and the adaptivity term \chi_t/\beta_t^{1.5} ~ t^{1.5\beta-\chi} decays more slowly than the batch-means rate (t\beta_t)^{-1/4} = t^{-(1-\beta)/4} whenever 1.5\beta < \chi < 1.5\beta + (1-\beta)/4, a nonempty sub-regime of the theorem's own hypothesis \chi>1.5\beta. Example: \beta=0.6, \chi=0.95 (satisfying \chi>1.5\beta=0.9) gives \hat{\Xi}_t's bound t^{-0.05}, slower than the batch-means t^{-0.1}. The asserted universal ordering is therefore false as stated; it holds only when the adaptivity error is higher order, i.e., \chi \geq 2\beta (in particular deterministic stepsizes), where 1/\sqrt{t\beta_t} indeed dominates (t\beta_t)^{-1/4} for all \beta\in(0.5,1).

failure_location.quote: the aforementioned works all showed that the convergence rate of the batch-means estimators is $O(1/\sqrt[4]{t\beta_t})$, which is slower than that of $\hat{\Xi}_t$~in~\mbox{Theorem}~\ref{sec4:thm1}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the comparison to \chi \geq 2\beta (or deterministic stepsizes), the regime the paper itself singles out as making the adaptivity error higher order.
issues.overall_effect: A comparative-advantage claim used to position the estimator against first-order batch-means estimators is overstated for part of the advertised adaptive-stepsize regime; no formal result is affected.
issues.title: Blanket claim that the batch-means rate O((t beta_t)^{-1/4}) is slower than \hat{\Xi}_t's rate fails when chi is close to 1.5 beta
issues.why_classification: A short local qualification of a discussion claim restores correctness; the paper's formal guarantees and the comparison in the central regime (deterministic stepsize or \chi\geq2\beta, as used in the experiments) survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The second inequality is due to $\|C_k-C^\star\|\leq \tau\Upsilon_{S}^{1/2}\|B_k-B^\star\|/\gamma_H$ \cite[Lemma 5.2]{Na2022Statistical}

failure_location.quote: Notably, Theorem \ref{sec4:thm1} does~not~\mbox{require}~$B_t$~to~\mbox{converge}~to~the true Hessian $\nabla^2 F(\tx)$, making our analysis directly applicable to conditioned SGD methods.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either withdraw/soften the bullet to an open direction, or carry out the extension: redo the decomposition with drift (I-\bar C)\bar B^{-1}B* (without the symmetric eigendecomposition argument) and re-derive the consistency of the weighted sample covariance for the corresponding limiting covariance.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised applicability of \hat{\Xi}_t as a consistent covariance estimator for conditioned SGD methods (explicitly including AdaGrad, RMSProp, and quasi-Newton) is unsubstantiated; the main results for (sketched) Newton methods are unaffected.
issues.title: Claim that Theorem sec4:thm1's analysis 'directly' covers conditioned SGD contradicts the proof's essential use of B_t -> nabla^2 F(x*)
issues.why_classification: No short routine fix exists: substantiating the claim requires a contained but nontrivial rework of the core decomposition (Lemmas appen:A4:lem1-appen:A5:lem1) with a different drift structure, while deleting the bullet withdraws an advertised application; the central theorems remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we let $\mF_t = \sigma(\{\xi_i\}_{i=0}^t)$, for any $t\geq 0$, be the filtration~of~$\sigma$-algebras generated by the sample sequence $\xi_0, \xi_1,\xi_2\ldots$.

issues.failure_explanation: x_t is generated via \barDelta x_{t-1} = \Delta x_{t-1,\tau}, which depends on the sketching matrices S_{t-1,j}, and B_t involves the x_i; hence neither x_t nor B_t is measurable with respect to the defined F_{t-1} = \sigma(\xi_0,...,\xi_{t-1}), which contains no sketching randomness (indeed x_t is not even F_t-measurable). Consequently the stated conditional-expectation identities are false as written - e.g., in Lemma aux:lem4(b) the right-hand side -(I-C_t)B_t^{-1}\nabla F_t is random given F_{t-1} and cannot equal the F_{t-1}-measurable left-hand side - and throughout the proofs (e.g., (appen:A2:equ4)) \nabla F_t, B_t, C_t are pulled out of \mE[\cdot\mid\mF_{t-1}] as if they were F_{t-1}-measurable; likewise C_t = \mE[\tilde C_t\mid\mF_{t-1}] no longer coincides with the pathwise object used in the recursion bounds.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Enlarge the filtration to include the sketching randomness, e.g., \mF_t = \sigma(\{\xi_i\}_{i\leq t}, \{S_{s,j}\}_{s\leq t, j}); then x_{t+1}, B_{t+1} \in \mF_t, the sampling/sketching independence properties are preserved, and every argument goes through verbatim with no change to statements or rates.
issues.overall_effect: Every result proved by conditioning on \mF_{t-1} is formally invalid under the stated filtration: aux:lem4 and, downstream, Theorems sec3:thm1 and sec3:thm2, Lemma sec4:lem1, Theorem sec4:thm1, Corollary sec4:cor1, and the appendix lemmas appen:A4:lem1-appen:A4:lem5 and appen:A5:lem1-appen:A5:lem4.
issues.title: Filtration is defined only over the samples xi, but iterates and Hessian averages also depend on sketching randomness, so the conditional-expectation formalism is invalid as written
issues.why_classification: The defect is repaired by a standard one-line enlargement of the filtration; all methods, conclusions, rates, and advertised scope survive unchanged, with no new lemma or altered argument.
